documents.summary: Tier 1. Fall 2026 syllabus for UTSA's first programming course for CS majors (instructor Mauricio Alejandro Gomez Morales). Its GenAI Use Policy bans GenAI for all work before the first exam, then allows it only as a learning and debugging aid, with lists of permitted and banned uses. Students must be able to explain and demonstrate any submitted work, and failing to do so may count as an integrity violation. documents.title: CAP 4111 Introduction to Augmented & Virtual Reality (Fall 2026 syllabus)
documents.summary: Tier 1. Fall 2026 syllabus for a Bellini College computing course (instructor Zhao Han) with a full 'Acceptable Use of Generative AI Tools' policy. GenAI is allowed for all submissions, as in the workplace, but students must verify output, cite all AI content and use AI only as a supplement. Copying AI code or writing is not allowed, misuse brings penalties up to program dismissal under USF and Bellini integrity policy, and assignments where AI is inappropriate will be marked. Identical code from the same AI prompt also counts as plagiarism, and any plagiarism brings an F for the lab and possibly the course. Its AI Policy treats AI as an assistive professional tool, requires it for some assignments, and lists appropriate uses (brainstorming, grammar, debugging help when noted) and inappropriate ones (whole coding solutions, unedited output). Students must acknowledge and describe any AI use and be able to explain their work; undisclosed AI-generated work counts as plagiarism under a graduated penalty scheme. documents.title: CEN 3024C 13038 Software Development I (Fall 2026 syllabus)
documents.summary: Tier 1. Fall 2026 syllabus for Valencia's Software Development I (instructor Lisa Macon). It allows AI chatbots for research and debugging on marked assignments but bans GitHub Copilot and other coding copilots, arguing that developers must be able to write their own code. It sets six ethical practices: verify accuracy, use AI as a tool not a crutch, watch for bias, protect privacy, disclose use, and follow no-AI instructions. The college's template 'Academic Integrity and Use of AI' block is also included. Text retrieved via the Simple Syllabus platform's public JSON endpoint for this public syllabus page.
